target_customer: Donors and people seeking high-impact careers and causes; funded by philanthropic donors rather than customers
problem: Donors and altruistic people lack evidence-based guidance on where to give money or time for the most good.
business_model: Nonprofit funded by grants and donations

founders.name: William MacAskill
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/President on the YC page; the CEA site names him as founder of the effective altruism movement.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly websites, community programs and grantmaking; no hard engineering problem.

defensibility.rationale: The effective altruism brand and community are hard to copy, but the nonprofit has no technical barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent tried to absorb it. In January 2024 CEA announced separation from Effective Ventures per a summary page, an internal restructuring.

market_need_then: CEA's own page says it entered YC's nonprofit program in December 2016; the Open Philanthropy grant of March 2017 shows institutional donor demand.

branding.name_origin: Formed in 2012 by merging Giving What We Can and 80,000 Hours under one registered organisation; one account says the name came after a long naming process.
branding.domain_note: Public site effectivealtruism.org, which is the movement's site run by CEA.

identity.voice_and_tone: Evidence and reasoning focused per its site

branding.brand_signature: The term effective altruism itself, first agreed on in a 2012 community naming discussion per one source

rebrands.why: A summary page says the umbrella entity renamed to reduce confusion

branding.community_and_virality: Site reports hundreds of thousands engaged and over 11,000 pledges to give 10 percent of income.

brand_strength.rationale: The movement name became widely known and the pledge count is large, though this is the movement brand more than CEA itself.

outcome_analysis: CEA is a nonprofit that went through YC in Winter 2017, received a 2.5 million dollar Open Philanthropy general support grant in March 2017 and ran programs such as EA Grants. It continued as a leading community-building organisation, restructuring in 2024 to separate from Effective Ventures. It is not a venture outcome, so success is judged by donor backing and brand reach.
notes: Open Philanthropy lists $2.5M; a tracker lists $3M. The grant is cross-checked by CEA's own blog post announcing it. Other co-founders such as Toby Ord appear only in search snippets I did not open, so are not listed as founders. Competitor sources found were undated or from 2013 and 2025, so the list is empty. The April 2025 'no longer effective' post is an April Fools joke.
